text:
jordan: Heads up — internal inference API in us-west-2 started failing liveness checks for GPU nodes around 12:10. ELB marking targets unhealthy.
sasha: seeing the same. healthchecks to nodePort 30010 time out from LB. pods are Running, kube-probes look OK from inside cluster.
liam: I can reproduce from a jumpbox: tcpdump on node shows SYN from LB, but no SYN-ACK back. SGs look fine for 30010.
noor: digging in — I pushed a NACL change last night to block a weird outbound CIDR. did it land on the edge subnets? :facepalm:
jordan: can you paste the acl id/rule? rolling changes now?
noor: acl is acl-0abc1234 us-west2-edge-subnet. New deny rule has ruleNumber 100 blocking ports 32768-60999 TCP to 0.0.0.0/0. I meant to scope it to a host range but used 0.0.0.0/0 by mistake.
liam: that explains it — ELB healthchecks use ephemeral ports for return path. NACL DENY with lower rule number takes precedence, so connection gets dropped after SYN.
sasha: quick proof: from nat-jumpbox i can telnet to node:30010 and it connects, but from LB we see SYN but no response. tcpdump on NAT shows return attempts being dropped at subnet boundary.
noor: rolling back now: `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abc1234 --rule-number 100 --protocol tcp --port-range From=32768,To=60999 --egress YES --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --rule-action ALLOW`
devops-bot: Incident #INC-2026 created: edge-nacl-blocking-lb-healthchecks — assigned to noor, severity P2.
jordan: after the replace, ELB target health started ticking to healthy within 30s. Marking incident mitigated but not resolved until postmortem.
liam: action items: 1) revert that deny to a scoped CIDR in terraform (no manual one-offs), 2) add TF guardrail/policy to block NACL denies that include ephemeral port ranges for egress on edge subnets, 3) add automated test that simulates LB -> node ephemeral handshake on deploys.
sasha: also add a runbook note: prefer security groups + NAT gateway controls for outbound filtering rather than node-subnet NACL denies that can break return paths.
noor: agreed. Sorry for the outage — will open a PR with the scoped deny and the policy checks. link to quick diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482
jordan: thanks. tagging oncall for follow-up: @liam can you include this in weekly infra retro and ensure owners are aware.
liam: will do, and I'll attach packet captures and NACL rule history to the postmortem.
devops-bot: @channel Incident updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Follow-up task created: TF-guardrails-197.
